reviewAdvisory: The 12-14 per year figure is derived by dividing 20 simultaneous berths by a 16-month build time, but the figures do not state that all berths are occupied, that build time is uniform across the order book, or that the 16-month record is the standard cycle — the draft itself later admits 16 months may be exceptional.

The supplied figures only support a record for Hudong-Zhonghua (12th delivery, 14 expected); the draft upgrades this to a record for Chinese shipbuilders as a class without any figure covering other yards.
The figures record 17 new orders but do not identify who placed them; the draft elsewhere admits the report does not state who placed the orders, so attributing them to charterers is invented.
The body performs arithmetic (20 berths ÷ 16 months = 12-14 vessels per year) and the 'How we calculated this' section denies any arithmetic was done, contradicting the body.
The 'mid-sized city for about a month' and the −162°C figure are not in the supplied figures and carry no five-part record, so they are unsourced numbers in the prose.
This is a general market assertion with no figure or document behind it; the draft's own figures contain no charter-rate or demand data, so the causal rule is unsupported.
